text:
sam: Ran an nsys trace on the new kv-prefetch change, putting the trace and a quick TL;DR here. Timeline looks like memcpy/host copies are frequently serializing kernels and there are 10-30ms CPU scheduling gaps tied to the prefetch worker.

sam: command: `nsys profile -o out/kvtrace --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt python -m bench.prefetch_trace`

sam: timeline snippet (abridged):
```
GPU stream 0: [kernel A][kernel B][kernel C]         [kernel D]
GPU stream 1: [memcpy H2D ---- blocking ----][kernel E]
Host CPU: prefetch_worker ---sleep(15ms)--- wake --- memcpy submit
Total tokens: 512, batcher window: 8ms
Observed: repeated small kernels (~1.2ms) and frequent host-to-device memcpy stalls that coincide with kernel gaps.
```

sam: nsys summary: memcpy H2D accounted for 28% of GPU time, kernels 62%, host blocked time ~15% across timeline.

maria: :eyes: do we have whether the memcpy is using pinned memory? pageable H2D will block and sync with kernels more often.

alex: Also noticed after last kernel-selection tweak we split fused fwd kernel into two, so more kernel launches and fewer ops per launch. That + small batches = lots of tiny kernels and host pressure.

ion: hypothesis: prefetch worker scheduling + pageable allocations = host threads getting preempted, then when they wake they push a big memcpy that blocks stream and waits on CPU, causing the observed 10-30ms holes.

kim: quick experiment: turned on pinned pool (cudaHostAlloc with pooled allocator) + bumped batcher aggregation window from 8ms -> 18ms on a single node. Re-ran a short trace.

kim: results (single-run): p50 latency went 48ms -> 33ms, p95 180ms -> 110ms, throughput +18%. memcpy % GPU time dropped from 28% -> 10%.

alex: nice. That suggests two knobs: (1) avoid pageable host copies (pinned pool) and (2) increase batching window so kernels are less chatty. We should still validate memory pressure and latency tail for very low qps.

maria: can we also try keeping the fused kernel path as fallback for small batch sizes? cheaper to launch one big kernel occasionally than many tiny launches.

sam: I can prototype: change kernel selector to prefer fused if batch_size < 4 or if last N windows had >30% memcpy stalls.

ion: also add affinity/cgroup tweak for prefetch worker so it doesn't get preempted behind heavy OS tasks. Put it on isolated CPU or nice -20? maybe too aggressive.

perfbot: perf CI run queued: https://perf.redwood/ci/kvtrace/171950. Attaching flamegraph and perfetto link once complete.

kim: FYI the quick pinned pool run increased host memory by ~400MB but stays within node footprint for our test instance. We'll want dynamic fallback when memory is tight.

sam: action items:
- kim: run 10-run A/B with pinned pool vs pageable on 3 instance sizes (small/medium/large) and post p50/p95/throughput.
- alex: prototype fused-kernel fallback in selector and run microbench to measure launch overhead tradeoffs.
- ion: try worker CPU affinity change on one perf node and rerun nsys to confirm reduction in scheduling gaps.
- maria: create perf regression ticket and tag EngRuntime/KB-Perf.

maria: I'll file the ticket now and include these numbers + the nsys trace. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks, folks. If we see consistent improvement we'll add pinned-pool to default batcher config behind a runtime flag and ship a rollout to canary.

alex: one extra note: watch KV cache eviction churn—larger batching + pinned pool might increase resident memory and change eviction patterns. Keep an eye on cache hit rates.

kim: posted initial 10-run CSV to GCS: gs://redwood-perf/kv-prefetch/pinned_vs_pageable/171950. I'll update when the 30-run suite is done.

sam: linking the nsys capture tar: gs://redwood-perf/kv-prefetch/nsys/171950_kvtrace.tar.gz

perfbot: CI results uploaded: https://perf.redwood/reports/171950-kv-prefetch (perfetto + waterfall screenshots attached).
